memos.headline: AAPL Overbought at 52-Week Highs While XOM and PG Break Down on Relative Strength
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. AAPL is trading within 0.1% of its 52-week high with an RSI of 78.8 and sits 13.4% above its 50-day mean — a textbook overbought condition that warrants caution despite the powerful trend. AMZN and UNH look like the cleanest intermediate-term setups: both are near highs with strong 12-week relative strength vs SPY (+14.4% and +19.8% respectively) yet carry RSIs in the high-50s, leaving room to run. On the downside, XOM is the weakest name in the group with RSI 38.6, a -6.5% weekly return, -15.3% drawdown from highs, and -11.1% 4-week relative strength vs SPY — a clear breakdown. PG is similarly weak, sitting 15.5% off its high with -19.7% 12-week relative strength, confirming persistent distribution.

views.note: RSI 78.8 and +13.4% above 50d mean screams overbought; I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50d (~275) before getting involved.
Near 52-week highs with only -1.6% drawdown, RSI 59.7 not yet stretched, and +14.4% 12w relative strength vs SPY; would reverse below the 50d mean (~246).
Strongest 12-week relative strength in the universe at +19.8% vs SPY with RSI 57.8 offering room; invalidated on a close below 360.
RSI 38.6, -6.5% weekly loss, -15.3% off highs, and worst 4w/12w relative strength in the group — clear downtrend; would reconsider only above the 50d mean (~155).
Persistent weakness with -19.7% 12w relative strength vs SPY, below both 50d and 200d means, and -15.5% drawdown from highs.
Strong 1w +7.4% surge pushing RSI to 69.6 suggests momentum ignition off a -16.9% drawdown base, but still below the 200d mean — needs follow-through above 460 for conviction.
RSI 49.4 is dead neutral and 4w relative strength vs SPY is flat at +0.5%; no edge either way until it reclaims 220 or breaks 195.
Negative 4w and 12w relative strength vs SPY (-9.7% and -10.4%), below both moving averages, and RSI 45.7 trending lower — no reason to own.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Post Extraordinary Earnings Growth; XOM and UNH Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I am struck by the sheer dispersion in earnings quality across this universe. NVDA's 2027Q1 filing shows $81.6B in revenue (+85% YoY) and a 71.5% net margin producing $58.3B of net income (+211% YoY) on only $8.5B of total debt — this is the cleanest earnings power profile I have seen in years. GOOGL delivered $62.6B of net income on $109.9B of revenue (+22% YoY) at a 56.9% net margin with minimal leverage ($14.8B debt), while MSFT printed 38.3% net margins and +23% net income growth on $82.9B of revenue. On the other side, XOM's net income collapsed 46% YoY to $4.2B on a 4.9% net margin, and UNH's earnings were essentially flat (-0.2%) on anemic 2% revenue growth with $77.9B of debt — both signal durable earnings compression risk. CAT surprised positively with +22% revenue growth and +27% net income growth, though I want to see whether the cyclical tailwind persists before adding conviction.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, net margin 71.5%, net income +211% YoY on minimal $8.5B debt — unmatched earnings power; would reassess if margins fall below 55%.
Net income +81% YoY to $62.6B at 56.9% margin with only $14.8B debt is exceptional operating leverage; a deceleration in ad revenue growth below 10% would change my view.
Revenue +18% YoY, net margin 38.3%, and net income +23% with manageable $40.3B debt demonstrate durable cloud-driven earnings growth.
Net income surged 77% YoY to $30.3B and margin expanded to 16.7%, but $122.6B of total debt keeps me at moderate confidence; margin contraction below 12% would flip me neutral.
Solid +17% revenue growth and 26.6% net margin, but $82.7B debt load and slower earnings growth (+19%) relative to mega-cap peers warrant a neutral stance until I see services mix acceleration.
Revenue +22% and net income +27% are impressive, but cyclical industrials with $36.2B debt need sustained backlog evidence before I commit; a revenue decline in Q2 would push me to avoid.
Revenue +10% and net income +12.6% at a 33.1% margin are respectable for a bank, but the $449B debt structure and rate-cycle sensitivity limit upside conviction.
Steady 18.5% net margin and +7.4% revenue growth offer defensive ballast, but +4.3% earnings growth barely keeps pace with inflation; I need margin expansion to get constructive.
Net income down 46% YoY to $4.2B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin signals commodity-driven earnings compression; would reconsider only if margins recover above 10%.
Flat net income (-0.2%) on just 2% revenue growth with $77.9B of debt points to structural margin pressure in managed care; need to see medical-loss ratio improvement to revisit.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% but Sticky 3.8% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue for Caution on Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see a clear pause regime: the Fed has held the upper bound at 3.75% for three months after cutting 75bp over the prior year, and the April CPI print shows headline inflation running at 3.8% YoY—well above target and likely keeping the FOMC sidelined through summer. The 10-year yield has jumped 48bp over three months to 4.45%, flattening the 10y-2y spread to just 46bp, which signals the market is repricing term premium higher and pushing back on further easing. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.3%, unchanged over three months and only 10bp higher YoY, so there is no recession catalyst to force the Fed's hand. This combination—sticky inflation, rising long rates, stable employment—favors short-duration value and financials over long-duration growth names, and I would be cautious on rate-sensitive cyclicals like housing-exposed industrials. A CPI print dropping below 3.0% YoY or unemployment breaching 4.6% would flip my regime call toward renewed easing.

views.note: Banks benefit from a positive-slope curve (46bp 10y-2y), stable credit conditions with 4.3% unemployment, and a prolonged pause that keeps NIM healthy.
Rising 10y yields at 4.45% pressure high-multiple growth names, but secular AI demand provides an offset; I lack conviction either way until rates stabilize.
Duration headwind from the 48bp 3-month rise in the 10y yield tempers upside, though consumer spending resilience from low unemployment provides a floor.
Same duration drag as other mega-cap growth; sticky CPI and a paused Fed mean no near-term multiple expansion catalyst.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a pause-with-sticky-inflation regime; PG's pricing power helps pass through 3.8% YoY CPI.
Stable macro with no recession signal supports energy demand, but rising real rates and no clear growth acceleration limit upside conviction.
Cyclicals face headwinds from higher long-end rates squeezing capex financing; the 48bp 3-month rise in the 10y is a direct drag on equipment orders.
Consumer-facing strength from 4.3% unemployment is offset by long-duration valuation pressure from 4.45% 10y yields.
Ad spending should hold up with stable employment, but no rate-cut catalyst means limited multiple expansion for high-growth tech.
Defensive healthcare with stable demand regardless of rate regime; benefits from pause environment where investors rotate toward quality.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: GOOGL and CAT Surged, MSFT and NVDA Sold Off — Narrative Momentum Favors the Winners
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available. GOOGL (+10.0%) and CAT (+9.9%) posted outsized positive reactions on their Q1 results, suggesting a genuine narrative shift that likely attracted incremental media coverage and positive tone — these moves are large enough that sentiment momentum should persist near-term, though some of the easy upside is now priced. MSFT (-3.9%) and NVDA (-1.8%) saw negative reactions to their earnings, and MSFT's subsequent director departure filing on 5/14 adds a layer of uncertainty that could keep tone negative. UNH's +7.0% earnings pop was notable but the subsequent Reg FD filing on 5/11 without a price tag leaves me less certain the positive tone is building further. JPM's muted -0.8% reaction and heavy governance-related filing activity (bylaws amendments, material modification to security-holder rights) suggest a noisy, neutral-to-cautious media backdrop rather than a clear directional signal.

views.note: A +10.0% earnings-day pop is a powerful positive tone catalyst; follow-through 8-K filings in May suggest continued newsflow, though some upside is now priced.
The +9.9% earnings reaction signals a sharp positive sentiment turn for a cyclical name; tone should stay supportive near-term.
A -3.9% earnings selloff followed by a director departure filing two weeks later keeps sentiment tone negative and uncertain.
The -1.8% post-earnings dip is modest and two prior director-change filings add noise; sentiment is mixed rather than clearly negative.
A +7.0% earnings pop was strong but the subsequent Reg FD filing without visible price impact leaves me only moderately confident the positive tone persists.
Flat earnings reaction and heavy governance filings (bylaws, material rights modifications) create a noisy backdrop with no clear sentiment direction.
A +3.2% earnings reaction is modestly positive; director change filing adds minor noise but overall tone turned constructive.
A -1.0% earnings dip and a subsequent director departure suggest mildly negative sentiment tone, though conviction is low.
A tepid +0.8% earnings reaction and routine shareholder-vote filing suggest sentiment is flat; no clear narrative shift.
A +1.7% earnings pop is in line with defensive expectations; tone is stable but not exciting enough to drive further upside.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty and Surging Oil Prices Signal Persistent Geopolitical Risk Despite Falling VIX
memos.body: I see a bifurcated risk picture as of today. The economic policy uncertainty index at 279.84 has dropped 27.8% over the past month but remains 86.5% above its level three months ago, suggesting that while the acute phase of a policy shock may be fading, the structural overhang—likely tied to trade/sanctions actions—persists. WTI crude at $92.65 is up a striking 38.4% over three months even as it has pulled back 10.4% in the last month, consistent with an energy-security disruption (sanctions enforcement, supply restrictions, or conflict premium) that has only partially unwound. Credit spreads (HY OAS at 2.72%, tightening) and VIX at 15.74 (down ~21% over 3m) tell me markets are pricing a de-escalation, but I am less sanguine given the still-elevated policy uncertainty baseline. My conviction is highest on names with direct exposure to energy-security tailwinds (XOM) and supply-chain/tariff headwinds (AAPL, CAT), and I remain cautious on companies whose China-facing revenue or hardware supply chains leave them vulnerable to any re-escalation of export controls or tariffs.

views.note: WTI up 38% in 3 months provides a structural energy-security tailwind; any further sanctions enforcement or supply disruption extends the premium.
Hardware supply-chain concentration in China and elevated policy uncertainty (+86.5% over 3m) make AAPL vulnerable to any re-escalation of export controls or tariffs.
Chip export controls remain the key structural geopolitical risk; with policy uncertainty still far above 3-month-ago levels, any tightening of AI-chip restrictions would hit NVDA disproportionately.
CAT benefits from infrastructure spending but faces tariff headwinds on steel/components; multiple 8-K filings in April suggest the company is actively managing disclosure around these risks.
Tightening credit spreads and a positive yield curve (10y-2y at 0.46pp) support bank earnings; sanctions-related transaction flows could add fee income, though a policy re-escalation is a risk.
Defensive staples name with limited direct geopolitical exposure, but elevated input costs from high oil prices and potential tariff pass-through keep me from getting constructive.
